title: Proactive burst replenishment and tenant fairness guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A production escalation from two customers surfaced a class of reserved-pool shortfalls where the autoscaler failed to replenish burst credit fast enough and the tenant fairshare allocator subsequently evicted warm tenants to cold pools. Symptoms observed: sudden 50-200ms latency spikes, elevated error rates for small-tenanted heavy-burst workloads, and reserved-pool depletion alerts at 03:12 UTC.

Investigation findings (what we know):
- Autoscaler smoothing window (default 2m) suppressed short, high-amplitude surge signals used for preemptive warmup. This caused a 60–90s delay before scale-up decisions.
- A separate burst-credit accounting edge case left visible 'stale' credits stuck in tenant ledgers; global pool had usable headroom that was not auto-rebalanced.
- Fairshare allocator treats tenants with <X qps as low-priority; combined with eviction heuristics we observed repeated warm-to-cold transitions for mid-size tenants after they burned burst credits.
- Canary telemetry gaps: the "burst_replenish_success" metric was not emitted for a subset of scale-up flows, blocking alert correlation.

Immediate mitigations applied (done during incident):
- Manually injected 2x burst credits into impacted tenant accounts to restore service. (Runbook step: manual_burst_replenish_v1, link below)
- Temporary reduction of autoscaler smoothing to 30s via runtime feature flag to reduce scale-up latency. Deployed to region eu-west-1 as a targeted hotfix.
- Emergency change to eviction threshold to avoid cold-pool migration for tenants with recent N-minute activity.
- Customer comms: account owners notified and support tickets elevated; status page updates published.

Root cause hypothesis and trade-offs considered:
- Root cause: combination of (a) oversmoothed scale signal missing short spikes and (b) conservative fairshare eviction logic that prioritizes reclaiming hot slots rather than leveraging global headroom.
- Trade-offs: lowering smoothing reduces false-positive scale-ups which increase cost. Manual replenishment is fast but operationally heavy. Automatic aggressive replenishment risks oversubscription during multi-region storms.

Proposed long-term fix (multiple coordinated workstreams):
1) Replenishment loop: implement a proactive replenishment controller that detects global headroom and atomically transfers burst credits to starving tenants during emergency thresholds. (Design doc: Confluence: /d/capacity/replenishment-controller)
2) Autoscaler policy changes: split the smoothing windows by signal type (short-burst vs sustained-load). Introduce an adaptive aggressiveness parameter based on recent false-positive rate.
3) Fairness guardrails: add a temporary "warmback" lease that prevents eviction for tenants who consumed burst credit < 5m ago. Also add weighting tweak to avoid starving medium tenants behind many tiny tenants.
4) Observability: emit new metrics (burst_replenish_attempt, burst_replenish_success, autoscaler_spike_detected) and add Grafana panels + SLO-aligned alerts.
5) QA + rollout: synthetic burst generator (k8s job) for automated regression tests; chaos test to simulate delayed replenish; staged rollout behind feature flags (canary 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100%).

Rollout plan and verification steps:
- Week 1 (this ticket): ship emergency replenishment circuit and observability additions behind feature flag; run in canary (5% tenants). Verify: no cold migrations for canary tenants during synthetic bursts, no sustained latency regressions.
- Week 2: enable autoscaler short-burst window and fairness guardrail in canary; run 12h soak and cost analysis.
- Week 3: progressive rollout to all dedicated regions with monitoring and rollback playbook.

Testing and acceptance criteria:
- Synthetic load: generator reproduces 90% of field spikes, 95th p99 latency remains below baseline under burst.
- Telemetry: burst_replenish_success > 99% for triggered events in canary and alerts fire correctly for failures.
- Cost: expected short-term increase in peak capacity < 7% for canary. Approve with PM if >10%.
